knowledge_base.description: Cross-Site Scripting attacks occur when malicious scripts are injected into otherwise trusted websites. An attacker can use XSS to send a malicious script to an unsuspecting user.
knowledge_base.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Go to Collection Details.
2. Enter the necessary details.
3. Intercept the request.
4. Replace the remarks value with an XSS payload.
5. Observe that it is stored and executed in the browser.
knowledge_base.remediation:
1. Filter input on arrival.
2. Encode data on output.
3. Use appropriate response headers.
4. Implement Content Security Policy.

knowledge_base.vulnerability_name: Cross Site Scripting (XSS) via File Upload
knowledge_base.description: XSS through file upload occurs when uploaded content is insufficiently validated or encoded and can be interpreted as active content (e.g., SVG, HTML file upload).
knowledge_base.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Login using the provided credentials.
2. Navigate to the relevant module.
3. Upload a malicious file (e.g., test.svg with script).
4. Intercept and modify the request using Burp Suite.
5. Observe successful storage and rendering of the file.
knowledge_base.remediation:
1. Strictly validate uploaded files.
2. Validate content type and extension.
3. Store uploads outside executable web paths.
4. Encode output and serve with Content-Disposition: attachment.
5. Use Content Security Policy.

knowledge_base.description: The application uses the deprecated X-XSS-Protection HTTP response header. Modern browsers have removed support for this header because it can introduce security vulnerabilities in certain contexts.
knowledge_base.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Visit target URL: http://localhost:5173/report-generator
2. Intercept the request.
3. Send to Repeater.
4. Inspect the response headers.
knowledge_base.remediation:
1. Remove deprecated X-XSS-Protection header.
2. Implement Content Security Policy (CSP).
3. Implement input validation and output encoding.
4. Configure secure cookie settings.

knowledge_base.description: SQL injection is a web security vulnerability that allows an attacker to interfere with the queries that an application makes to its database, allowing unauthorized data retrieval or modification.
knowledge_base.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Navigate to search or login parameter.
2. Inject payload: ' OR '1'='1.
3. Observe database error or authentication bypass.
knowledge_base.remediation:
1. Use parameterized queries / prepared statements for all SQL execution.
2. Use Object Relational Mapping (ORM) safely.
3. Enforce principle of least privilege on database accounts.

knowledge_base.description: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) enforces secure HTTPS connections, preventing Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) and SSL-stripping attacks.
knowledge_base.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Send a request to the application over HTTPS.
2. Analyze response headers.
3. Note absence of Strict-Transport-Security header.
knowledge_base.remediation: 1. Add Strict-Transport-Security header: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload.

knowledge_base.description: The application's Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policy reflects arbitrary origins or allows wildcard with credentials, enabling malicious third-party websites to extract sensitive user data.
knowledge_base.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Send request with header 'Origin: https://attacker.com'.
2. Check response for 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://attacker.com' and 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'.
knowledge_base.remediation:
1. Whitelist only trusted domains for CORS.
2. Do not reflect arbitrary Origin headers when Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is true.

knowledge_base.description: The application uses user-supplied input to access objects directly without proper access control checks, allowing unauthorized users to view or modify records belonging to other users.
knowledge_base.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Login as User A and view profile with ID 101.
2. Change request parameter ID to 102.
3. Observe unauthorized access to User B's sensitive data.
knowledge_base.remediation:
1. Implement robust server-side authorization checks on all resource endpoints.
2. Use non-sequential random identifiers (UUIDs) where applicable.

knowledge_base.description: The web page does not restrict framing via X-Frame-Options or Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors, enabling attackers to render the page inside a transparent iframe and trick users into clicking buttons.
knowledge_base.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Create an HTML file with <iframe src='TARGET_URL'></iframe>.
2. Open in browser and verify the application renders successfully within the iframe.
knowledge_base.remediation:
1. Configure 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or 'SAMEORIGIN'.
2. Implement Content Security Policy with 'frame-ancestors 'self''.

findings.vulnerability_name: Cross Site Scripting (XSS) via File Upload
findings.description: XSS through file upload occurs when uploaded SVG/HTML content is insufficiently validated or sanitized.
findings.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Navigate to Map Layer Upload.
2. Upload malicious SVG payload with embedded script.
3. Verify script execution when layer is previewed.
findings.remediation:
1. Strictly validate file extensions and MIME types.
2. Serve uploaded assets with Content-Disposition: attachment.
3. Enforce strict Content Security Policy.

findings.description: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks.
findings.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Inspect HTTP response headers.
2. Note absence of Content-Security-Policy header.
findings.remediation: 1. Define and implement a robust Content-Security-Policy header restricting script-src and object-src.

findings.description: The application uses deprecated security header which modern browsers ignore.
findings.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Send request and inspect response headers.
2. Observe X-XSS-Protection header present.
findings.remediation: 1. Remove X-XSS-Protection header and use CSP instead.

findings.vulnerability_name: Insecure Data Storage in Shared Preferences
findings.description: Sensitive auth tokens and session keys stored unencrypted in local Android SharedPreferences.
findings.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Decompile APK with JADX.
2. Inspect shared_prefs/auth_session.xml.
3. Extract plain-text tokens.
findings.remediation:
1. Use Android EncryptedSharedPreferences (Jetpack Security).
2. Store cryptographic keys in Android Keystore System.

findings.description: The mobile app accepts self-signed SSL certificates without certificate pinning verification.
findings.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Configure Burp Suite CA certificate.
2. Intercept mobile app HTTPS traffic.
3. Verify all REST API payloads decrypted.
findings.remediation:
1. Implement Network Security Configuration with strict SSL Public Key Pinning.
2. Detect and terminate on Frida/Xposed hooks.

findings.vulnerability_name: Missing Root Detection & Runtime Integrity Protection
findings.description: Application does not verify if Android device is rooted or running in an emulated environment.
findings.steps_to_reproduce:
1. Launch app on rooted device.
2. Attach Frida agent to inspect runtime memory.
3. Bypass client-side security checks.
findings.remediation:
1. Implement Google Play Integrity API.
2. Add multi-layered Rootbeer & Magisk detection checks.
